title.description: Under 60 chars. Imperative action phrase (start with a verb), e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option". Shown as the chip label and the spawned session title.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

cwd.description: Optional. Absolute path to a different project root than the current session's — a path on the host this session runs on. The spawned session gets a fresh worktree under this path. Defaults to the current project — only set this when the work clearly belongs in another repo on that host.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

## plugin:parallel:parallel-search

The search and fetch tools are read-only, idempotent, and safe to call
concurrently. When several independent search or fetch objectives are already
known, issue one tool call per objective concurrently; do not wait for one
result before starting another. Batch related search queries or URLs that share
a common objective into one call.



Use web_search first for most factual, current-information, research,
comparison, documentation, and troubleshooting questions.

The web_search results include excerpts intended to be useful for answering
directly. If the excerpts contain enough evidence, answer from them — do not
fetch every search result by default. For broad tasks you can issue multiple
`search_queries` in a single web_search call rather than chaining calls.

Use web_fetch when the user asks about a specific URL or page, needs exact
wording or quotes, requests full-page analysis, or when search excerpts are
conflicting or clearly insufficient.



Use web_fetch only when web_search excerpts are not enough: the user asked
about a specific URL or page, you need exact wording or quotes, you need
full-page analysis, or the excerpts are conflicting or clearly insufficient.
Do not fetch every search result by default — search excerpts are usually
answer-ready.

When you do fetch, you can pass multiple related URLs in one call along with
a common `objective`; the tool will return the parts most relevant to it.


Use of this server is subject to the Parallel Customer Terms (https://parallel.ai/customer-terms) and Privacy Policy (https://parallel.ai/privacy-policy).

## plugin:small-business:shopify
This server helps users set up and manage their Shopify stores.

## Starting a New Business
Users who are still shaping a business can work on it here before they have a store. None of these tools needs one.
- Naming: generate-business-names suggests business names from a short description of what the user sells, who it is for, or the feeling they want.
- Domains: generate-domain-names checks whether a name or domain idea is available and what it costs to register, and suggests available alternatives.
When the user settles on a name, offer to check domains for it.
Never present a domain as available unless generate-domain-names checked it; a domain you suggest yourself may already be taken.
Follow the user's lead rather than walking them through every step.

## Store Creation
Users who don't have a store yet can use get-new-store-previews to create one from a short description.
After calling get-new-store-previews, encourage the user to browse the previews and pick the theme they like best.
Each preview has a signup link — signing up through it creates a real Shopify store with that theme and matching products pre-installed.
Encourage continued brainstorming: users can try different descriptions, tweak ideas, or explore new directions without commitment.

## Store Management
Once a store exists, this server provides tools for managing it:
- Products: search, create, update, bulk-update status, and organize into collections.
- Collections: search, create, update, and manage product groupings.
- Orders: list recent orders and get detailed order information.
- Customers: list and search customers.
- Inventory: check inventory levels and set quantities at specific locations.
- Analytics: run ShopifyQL queries for sales, order, and product performance data.
- Discounts: create percentage-based discount codes.

# Solo License **A driving license for AI agents.**
The agent starts by asking permission, earns freedom one verified job at a time, and is paused the instant something goes wrong — until a person reviews and resumes it. *Earned. Revocable. Priced.* Built for the [neatHack AI agent hackathon](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon) · uses **neatlogs**, **Entire** and **cfo.ai** · by [@JAYATIAHUJA](https://github.com/JAYATIAHUJA)
--- ## The problem Today you either watch every action an AI agent takes, or you let it run and hope. Agents also *lie by accident*: a tool says "Refund processed" while nothing moved. If you trust that response, the mistake reaches your customer. ## What Solo License does | | | |---|---| | **Starts cautious** | Every job type (refunds, store credit) begins at *Suggests only* or *Needs your OK*. | | **Checks, never trusts** | After every action the agent re-reads the database. The tool's "success" message is ignored. | | **Earns freedom** | After *N* double-checked jobs in a row, that job type moves up one level — automatically. | | **Stops instantly** | Any caught problem pauses that job type at once. Other job types keep their own level. | | **A person decides** | One evidence page shows what was meant, what happened and why it stopped. A person resumes it at a level they choose. | | **Everything is recorded** | Every permission change is a git commit (explainable with Entire); every run is a neatlogs trace. | ### The four levels | Level | In the app | What the agent may do alone | |---|---|---| | L0 | **Suggests only** | Nothing — it suggests, you act | | L1 | **Needs your OK** | Prepares each job; you approve with one click | | L2 | **Works alone up to $50** | Jobs under the limit; bigger ones wait for you | | L3 | **Works alone** | Everything, reviewed afterwards | ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 direction LR L0: Suggests only L1: Needs your OK L2: Works alone up to limit L3: Works alone Paused: Paused (acts as L0) L0 --> L1: N verified jobs L1 --> L2: N verified jobs L2 --> L3: N verified jobs L1 --> Paused: problem caught L2 --> Paused: problem caught L3 --> Paused: problem caught Paused --> L2: person reviews and resumes ``` --- ## Results ### Before / after — trusting the tool vs. checking the result 50 real runs through the worker with 20 % injected faults (seeded, reproducible):

| | Trust the tool | Solo License | |---|---|---| | False successes reaching a customer | **10 / 50** | **0 / 50** | | Verified success rate | 80 % | 100 % | | Problems caught and paused | 0 | 10 | | Mean / p95 latency per run | — | 84 ms / 320 ms | Reproduce: `python -m scripts.benchmark` → [`artifacts/benchmark.md`](artifacts/benchmark.md) ### Autonomy is a margin driver

From stated assumptions in [`cfo/model.py`](cfo/model.py) (10,000 actions/month, $45/h loaded cost): - Earning **L2** saves **$41,250 / month** in review time → **+20.3 % margin**. - Running a level the agent has *not* earned (blind full-auto) adds ~$18,000 / month in incidents → **−73.4 % margin**. The app recomputes this live from your own runs on the **Reports** page — the number visibly drops when a job type is paused. --- ## How one run works ```mermaid flowchart LR M[Customer message] --> I[Intake
LLM or rules] I --> L{License check} L -->|allowed| X[Execute tool] L -->|not allowed| S[Suggest / wait for OK] X --> V[Re-read database] V --> D{Matches intent?} D -->|yes| C[Clean run
+1 toward next level] D -->|no| P[Problem caught
pause job type] P --> E[Evidence page] --> H[Person resumes] C & P & H --> G[(git ledger commit)] I & X & V & D -.-> N[[neatlogs trace]] ``` *The model proposes, the license decides, the database proves.* The LLM only reads the message and writes a plan — it never decides what is allowed. Problems the safety checks catch: | Check | Plain meaning | |---|---| | `state_mismatch` | The tool said "done", but nothing changed | | `policy_breach` | The agent acted beyond its permission | | `missing_verification` | The result was never double-checked | | `duplicate_action` | The same action ran twice | | intake guard | The message tries to change the agent's rules ("ignore your rules…") → sent to a person | --- ## How the three hackathon tools are used ### neatlogs — the trust signal - Every run is one **workflow trace** (`solo-license`) with spans for `license.check → plan → tool → verify.readback → detection.*`; caught problems are marked as **error spans**. - LLM calls (Gemini, Claude, OpenAI) are wrapped with `neatlogs.wrap`, so the model call sits inside the same trace. - The evidence page deep-links to the trace. Code: [`sololicense/observability/`](sololicense/observability). ### Entire — the audit trail - Every promote / pause / resume is one scoped commit of [`ledger/license_ledger.jsonl`](ledger/license_ledger.jsonl) with the reason, run and trace id. - Entire checkpoints are enabled for Claude Code and Codex sessions ([`.entire/settings.json`](.entire/settings.json)). ```bash git log --oneline -- ledger/license_ledger.jsonl # how each job type earned and lost its license entire checkpoint explain # why a change was made entire graph impact --repo . --symbol execute_refund # what the side-effecting tool touches ``` ### cfo.ai — the margin story - [`cfo/model.py`](cfo/model.py) turns stated assumptions into a supervision-cost curve, over-promotion risk and a P&L; narrative in [`cfo/business_model.md`](cfo/business_model.md). - The plan with pricing, costs, revenue and runway (4 scenarios) is built in cfo.ai through its MCP from these files and the benchmark. --- ## Evidence for judges | Requirement | Where to find it | |---|---| | Real end-to-end agent task | Refund + store-credit worker: intake → license → execute → read-back → detections → dial ([`worker.py`](sololicense/agent/worker.py)); try it in **Try the agent** | | Two runs with compared numbers | [`artifacts/benchmark.md`](artifacts/benchmark.md) (10/50 → 0/50) · `python -m scripts.generate_evidence` for a single clean-vs-fault pair | | neatlogs traces / detections | Benchmark runs were exported to neatlogs; detections are error spans per run | | A failure and what the agent did next | Guided tour step 4–8: practice problem → paused → evidence → person resumes | | Entire checkpoints / graph | 26 ledger commits: `git log -- ledger/license_ledger.jsonl`; `entire checkpoint list` | | cfo.ai plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway) | [`cfo/`](cfo) + plan built in cfo.ai via MCP | | Commits during the hackathon | `git log --since=2026-10-10` | | Tests | `python -m pytest` — 70 tests (state machine, detections, worker, API, ledger isolation, intake safety) | --- ## Run it locally **Requirements:** Python 3.11+, Node 20+, git. ```bash pip install -r requirements.txt cp .env.example .env # SOLO_DEMO_MODE=1 is already on; keys are optional python -m sololicense.db.seed # demo orders; refunds start at L2, store credit at L1 uvicorn app.api:app --port 8000 # API npm --prefix frontend install npm --prefix frontend run dev # http://127.0.0.1:5174 ``` Open the app → **Try the demo** → type your name. On **Home**, click **Watch a 1-minute demo**: a guided tour opens each screen, highlights what matters and runs the whole loop for real. **Optional keys** (Settings → AI model / Connections, or `.env`): `GEMINI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` / any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` for remote traces, and a Slack/Discord webhook for pause alerts. Without a model the agent uses built-in rules — the safety is identical, because authority never comes from the model. Keys saved in Settings are encrypted at rest. For a deployment, turn demo mode off and issue role-based access codes with `SOLO_API_TOKENS` (`operator` < `approver` < `admin`). Set `SOLO_LEDGER_REPO=.` to commit license changes into this repository so Entire can explain them. | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `make test` | Run the test suite | | `make seed` | Reset the demo database | | `make benchmark` | Re-run the 50-run before/after benchmark | | `make charts` | Redraw the README charts from the latest data | | `make cfo` | Print the financial model | --- ## Architecture ``` frontend/ React app — sign-in, onboarding, Home, Try the agent, Activity, Reports, History, Settings app/api.py FastAPI adapter: sessions, roles, settings (encrypted secrets), dashboard sololicense/ agent/ intake (LLM or rules), planner, worker loop, tools domain/ pure license state machine + task-class registry services/ verification, license service, git ledger, evidence, economics, alerts observability/ neatlogs tracer + detection rules db/ SQLite schema, migrations, repositories cfo/ financial model and plan scripts/ benchmark, evidence pair, README charts ``` Dependencies point inward: `domain` has no I/O and is unit-tested on its own. ## Honest positioning Graduated autonomy is not new — AWS described "graduated autonomy" (Aug 2026), and there is research and practitioner work on earned permission ladders. Solo License does not claim the ladder. What it adds: **demotion driven by detections on verified side effects**, **one evidence page a person uses to resume**, and **the license level treated as a priced margin driver**. # Solo License product-ready demo design ## Purpose and success criteria Solo License must demonstrate a trustworthy refund agent, not merely a chat screen. A first-time evaluator must be able to enter a demo workspace, complete onboarding, run a safe refund, inject a fault, see automatic demotion and human recovery, and inspect an evidence packet. A prospective customer must be able to configure their own model provider and observability credentials without exposing secrets back to the browser. The implementation remains runnable with no paid key, hosted database, or cloud account. It uses the existing SQLite store for the single-machine demo only and keeps explicit seams for a later hosted authentication and database layer. ## Product scope ### Access and onboarding The client will have a clear **Try the demo** path and a **Connect an existing workspace** path. Try the demo obtains a local-only demo session from the API; it is never enabled in a production deployment. Existing-workspace access accepts a deployment-issued access token and stores it only in browser session storage. After access is established, onboarding collects workspace name, model provider, model connection test, safety rules, and demo/sample orders. The UI will clearly label deterministic mode as the no-key choice. It will not claim to create a multi-user account: true sign-up/sign-in is deferred until hosted authentication is configured. ### Model providers and secret handling The supported provider choices are: 1. Deterministic demo mode (no key). 2. Google Gemini using a Gemini API key and configurable model. 3. Anthropic. 4. OpenAI. 5. GLM or another OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with key, model, and HTTPS base URL supplied by the customer. Provider fields have one canonical metadata table in the frontend and matching allow-listed settings in the backend. API keys are posted only to the API, saved through the existing encryption mechanism, masked on every read, and never sent to logs or evidence packets. Connection tests make a minimal request and return only a bounded status message. ### Safety and evidence The existing licensed refund worker remains the source of truth: it enforces levels, idempotency, refund ceilings, verification, fault injection, automatic demotion, human approval, and evidence packets. neatlogs remains optional; when configured, it records the workflow trace and the UI states whether remote observability is active. The evidence view will remain usable with no neatlogs key. `cfo.ai` and Entire are hackathon/developer integrations, not customer API-key fields. The app will include an honest finance-review export/readout; cfo.ai can analyse that material through its OAuth MCP workspace once the team connects it. Entire is configured for code checkpoints and Graph. Trails waits for Entire's account-level feature flag and repository-admin toggles. ## Architecture and interfaces ### Backend `Config` gains Gemini and OpenAI-compatible provider settings. A provider resolver in the LLM intake module dispatches the current Anthropic/OpenAI calls, Gemini REST call, or OpenAI-compatible REST call. The resolver has a single `complete(config, prompt, max_tokens)` interface so intake and planner do not need provider-specific code. The API expands its setting allowlist, secret masking, serialization, validation, and connection-test construction. The demo-session endpoint is isolated from role-protected endpoints and enabled only by an explicit local-demo environment flag. It returns a short-lived configured demo token; no implicit unauthenticated fallback is permitted. ### Frontend The API wrapper reads a session token from a small access-session module and adds a Bearer header. The access screen is shown before onboarding or app routes when no token is present. The onboarding and Settings model form consume shared provider metadata so every provider exposes the right fields, placeholders, and masked-key hints. The route guard sends an un-onboarded workspace to onboarding and an onboarded workspace to the dashboard. ### Future hosted deployment seam The browser depends only on a token provider, and the API depends only on an authenticated `Actor`. A future hosted auth provider replaces the demo/token access flow without changing worker code. SQLite repositories remain behind their current service boundaries so PostgreSQL/Supabase can replace them later. No schema migration or cloud deployment is in this delivery. ## Error handling and security - Reject unsupported provider identifiers, blank required fields, and non-HTTPS custom endpoints before a request is made. - Treat failed model tests as recoverable configuration errors; never overwrite a saved key because a masked or blank field was submitted. - Use timeouts and response-size/error-message bounds on network providers. - Never ship a demo session endpoint with the demo mode flag enabled in a hosted deployment. - Continue to require server-side encryption for persisted secrets. ## Verification Tests will cover provider dispatch/config validation, provider secret masking, demo-session access boundaries, browser authorization header behavior, and the onboarding/provider-field flow. Existing refund state-machine, API-security, and secret-storage tests remain green. The frontend production build must pass. ## External prerequisites that cannot be manufactured in code - A Gemini API key is required only for live Gemini calls; deterministic mode keeps the demo runnable without one. - A GLM/OpenAI-compatible key, model name, and HTTPS base URL are required only for that provider. - A neatlogs ingest key enables remote traces; it is optional for the demo. - cfo.ai uses an authenticated OAuth MCP connection, not a customer-facing API key field. - Entire Trails requires the team to obtain the feature flag, then an admin to enable Runners, Auto build on push, and Trails for the GitHub repository.

"""Fault injector.

Translates an armed :class:`FaultMode` into concrete, deterministic effects on
a single run. Two faults, two failure signatures the detections are built to
catch:

    QUIET_FAILURE    -> suppress the DB write; the execute tool still "succeeds".
                        Verification then measures a zero delta → state_mismatch.
    POLICY_VIOLATION -> force the agent to attempt an auto-execution its license
                        does not permit → policy_breach.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass

from sololicense.db.repositories import faults as faults_repo
from sololicense.domain.models import FaultMode


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FaultEffects:
    """How an armed fault bends the next run."""

    mode: FaultMode
    suppress_write: bool      # tool claims success but SQLite is untouched
    force_auto_execute: bool  # attempt auto-exec regardless of the license
    skip_verification: bool   # execute but do not read SQLite back

    @property
    def active(self) -> bool:
        return self.mode is not FaultMode.NONE


def effects_for(mode: FaultMode) -> FaultEffects:
    """Pure mapping from an armed mode to its effects."""
    return FaultEffects(
        mode=mode,
        suppress_write=mode is FaultMode.QUIET_FAILURE,
        force_auto_execute=mode is FaultMode.POLICY_VIOLATION,
        skip_verification=mode is FaultMode.SKIP_VERIFICATION,
    )


class FaultInjector:
    """Thin service over the armed-faults repository."""

    def __init__(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
        self._conn = conn

    def arm(self, task_class: str, mode: FaultMode) -> None:
        faults_repo.arm(self._conn, task_class, mode)
        self._conn.commit()

    def peek(self, task_class: str) -> FaultMode:
        return faults_repo.peek(self._conn, task_class)

    def consume_effects(self, task_class: str) -> FaultEffects:
        """Read and clear the armed fault, returning its effects."""
"""Task-class registry.

A *task class* is one kind of side effect the agent can be licensed for. Each
class earns and loses autonomy on its own ladder, and each names the single
``orders`` column that is the authority on whether its side effect landed —
the verifier reads exactly that column back after every execution.

Adding a class means adding one entry here (plus the column in the schema);
the worker, verifier, API and UI all read this registry instead of assuming
"refund".
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskClassSpec:
    key: str
    label: str            # "Refund"
    verb: str             # "refund" — used in sentences ("refund $25 on ORD-1")
    description: str      # what the action does, for prompts and the UI
    effect_column: str    # orders.<column> that proves the side effect
    keywords: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # deterministic intake hints


TASK_CLASSES: dict[str, TaskClassSpec] = {
    "refund": TaskClassSpec(
        key="refund",
        label="Refund",
        verb="refund",
        description="return money to the customer's original payment method",
        effect_column="refunded_amount",
        keywords=("refund", "money back", "chargeback", "return"),
    ),
    "store_credit": TaskClassSpec(
        key="store_credit",
        label="Store credit",
        verb="issue store credit of",
        description="issue store credit the customer can spend on a future order",
        effect_column="credit_issued",
        keywords=("store credit", "credit", "voucher", "gift card", "coupon"),
    ),
}

DEFAULT_TASK_CLASS = "refund"


def get_spec(task_class: str) -> TaskClassSpec:
    try:
        return TASK_CLASSES[task_class]
    except KeyError as error:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown task class: {task_class!r}") from error


def classify_text(message: str) -> str:
    """Deterministic fallback: pick the class whose keywords appear first.

    Store credit wins over refund when both appear ("refund as store credit"),
    because it is the more specific request."""
    text = message.lower()
    for key in ("store_credit", "refund"):
        if any(word in text for word in TASK_CLASSES[key].keywords):
            return key
    return DEFAULT_TASK_CLASS

# Solo License — cfo.ai business model

**Thesis:** the license level is a margin driver. Supervision is the cost;
autonomy is the lever. Solo License makes autonomy *earned*, so you capture the
savings of high autonomy without paying the incident bill of over-trust.

All figures are produced by `cfo/model.py` (`python -m cfo.model`) from stated
assumptions, and the level mix is recomputed from real runs when a seeded
database is present (`measured_level_distribution`).

## Assumptions

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Fully-loaded ops analyst | $45/hour |
| Refund volume | 10,000 / month |
| Average refund value | $32 |
| Price per seat | $400 / month |
| Seats | 40 |
| Incident rate if over-promoted | 1.5% of auto runs |
| Incident cost (clawback + handling) | $120 / incident |
| Cash on hand | $180,000 |

## Supervision-cost curve (the margin driver)

Each rung cuts the human minutes per refund. Across 10,000 refunds/month:

| Level | Minutes/run | Cost/run | Monthly supervision |
|---|---|---|---|
| L0 — suggest only | 6.0 | $4.50 | $45,000 |
| L1 — draft + approve | 3.0 | $2.25 | $22,500 |
| L2 — auto under ceiling | 0.5 | $0.375 | $3,750 |
| L3 — full auto (audited) | 0.1 | $0.075 | $750 |

**Climbing L0 → L2 saves $41,250 / month in supervision.** That is the prize.

## Risk model — the cost of over-promotion

Autonomy the agent has *not* earned is not free. Running a rung too high turns
1.5% of auto runs into incidents at $120 each:

content.text:
Pura codebase padh liya (backend `sololicense/`, `app/api.py`, frontend, seed, benchmark, cfo). Seedha jawab: **abhi yeh ek hackathon demo hai, real product nahi.** Agent ka loop sach mein chalta hai, lekin jo data aur paisa woh "refund" karta hai, dono nakli hain. Neeche detail mein.

---

## 1. Aaj ek user app ko kaise use karta hai

1. **Landing page → "Try the demo"** → naam type karo. Backend ek local demo session de deta hai (`/api/session/demo`). Koi real signup/login nahi hai.
2. **Onboarding (6 steps):** workspace ka naam → AI model chuno (ya "simple rules", bina key ke) → safety rules (jaise $50 limit) → orders → connections → review.
3. **Orders step:** "Load sample orders" pe tick karo, ya haath se order number, customer aur amount type karo.
4. **"Try the agent" page:** customer ka email ya chat message **paste karna padta hai** (`AgentDesk.jsx:43` — "Give the agent a customer message").
5. Agent message padhta hai, license level check karta hai, phir action leta hai, sirf suggest karta hai, ya aapke OK ka wait karta hai.
6. **Fault switch** se aap jaan-boojh kar ek problem paida karte ho. Agent pakad leta hai, us job type ko pause kar deta hai, evidence page dikhata hai, aur ek insaan use resume karta hai.
7. **Reports, History, Activity** pages: levels, runs aur paise ki bachat dikhate hain.

## 2. Aapke har sawaal ka seedha jawab

| Sawaal | Code mein sach kya hai |
|---|---|
| **Data kahan se aata hai?** | Ek local SQLite file se. Orders ya to `seed.py` ke 5 nakli orders hain (Ada Lovelace, Grace Hopper…), ya user ne haath se type kiye hain. Customer message bhi haath se paste hota hai. |
| **Refund kaise hota hai?** | **Koi real paisa nahi hilta.** `execute_refund` (`sololicense/agent/tools.py`) bas SQLite mein `refunded_amount` column badha deta hai. Na Stripe, na Shopify, na koi bank. |
| **Import/export kahan se?** | **Hai hi nahi.** CSV import, Shopify sync, export, kuch bhi nahi. Sirf "Add an order" form hai. |
| **Demo data kahan se?** | `sololicense/db/seed.py`, onboarding ka "Load sample orders", aur `/api/reseed` + `/api/demo/top-up` endpoints. |
| **Connectors kya hain?** | Teen hain, aur teeno *side* ke kaam ke hain: (a) **LLM provider** (Gemini/Claude/OpenAI), jo sirf message padh kar order ID aur amount nikalta hai; (b) **neatlogs**, jo har run ka trace record karta hai; (c) **Slack/Discord webhook**, jo pause hone pe alert bhejta hai. **In mein se koi bhi data andar nahi laata, aur koi paisa nahi hilata.** |
| **Agent kaam karta hai?** | Haan, loop asli hai aur tested hai (70 tests): intake → license check → execute → database dobara padhna → detection → level upar/neeche → git ledger commit. Lekin woh ek nakli database pe chalta hai. |
| **Faults kahan se aate hain?** | Humare apne fault switch se (`faults/injector.py`). Benchmark "10/50 → 0/50" bhi humare khud ke daale hue faults pe hai. Matlab hum apni banayi hui galti khud pakad rahe hain. Judges ke liye theek hai, lekin customer ke liye proof nahi hai. |
| **ML model train karna padega?** | **Nahi.** LLM ka kaam bas message se `order_id`, `amount` aur `reason` nikalna hai. Bina model ke regex rules bhi yahi karte hain. Permission dene ka kaam state machine karti hai (`domain/license.py`), aur sach ka faisla database read-back se hota hai. Product ki value ML mein nahi, is safety layer mein hai. |
| **Evals kya hain?** | `scripts/benchmark.py` (50 runs, 20% nakli faults) aur intake ke tests (prompt-injection wale messages pakadna). Real evals abhi nahi hain (section 4 dekho). |

## 3. Hum bech kisko rahe hain?

Landing page kehta hai: *"Ops teams putting AI agents near money"* (`Hero.jsx:12`). Cfo model maan ke chalta hai: mahine ke 10,000 refunds, $45/hour analyst, 40 seats × $400.

Real duniya mein do raaste hain. Aapko ek chunna padega:

- **A) Refund agent for e-commerce stores:** Shopify/Stripe wala D2C brand jiski support team roz refund tickets nipta rahi hai. User ka flow aisa hoga: Shopify connect karo → Gmail/Zendesk/Gorgias connect karo → tickets apne aap aate hain → agent refund karta hai → level dheere-dheere upar jaata hai.
- **B) "License layer" for agent builders:** ek SDK ya middleware. Jo company apna agent bana rahi hai, woh apne har side-effect wale tool ko Solo License mein wrap karti hai: permission, verification, demotion aur evidence. Code ka design (`task_classes.py` registry, alag verifier) is raaste ke zyada kareeb hai.

**Meri recommendation:** demo ke liye **A** dikhao, kyunki woh samajhna aasaan hai. Pitch **B** ka karo, kyunki asli moat wahi hai.

## 4. Real product banane ke liye kya karna padega

1. **Ek asli money connector**, jo sabse zaroori hai. Stripe (Refunds API) ya Shopify (`refundCreate` mutation) OAuth ke saath. `execute_refund` real API call karega, aur verifier us API se refund ya order **dobara fetch karke** check karega. Wahi asli "read-back" hai.
2. **Ek ticket inbox connector:** Gmail, Zendesk ya Gorgias ka webhook → `/api/intake` apne aap chale, paste karne ki zaroorat na pade.
3. **Orders sync** connector se aaye. Manual form sirf fallback rahe.
4. **Asli failures pakadna:** API timeout, aadha refund, ek hi webhook ka do baar aana, currency mismatch. Fault switch sirf demo mode mein dikhe.
5. **Asli evals:**
   - intake accuracy: real ya public support tickets ka labelled set, jahan check ho ki order ID aur amount sahi nikla;
   - prompt-injection set: dekhna ki kitne pakde gaye aur kitne galti se block hue;
   - detection precision/recall: Stripe test mode mein asli failures pe.
6. **Kya uthaya ja sakta hai (open source / existing):** Stripe aur Shopify ke official SDKs. Ticket intake ke liye Zendesk/Gorgias APIs. Policy ke liye OPA ya Cedar, agar rules complex ho jayein. Traces ke liye neatlogs already hai. **Koi model train nahi karna**; ek normal LLM extraction ke liye kaafi hai.

**Ek line mein:** engine (license, verify, demote, evidence) ban chuka hai aur kaam karta hai. Jo missing hai woh hai **pipes**: asli orders andar laana, asli tickets andar laana, aur asli paisa bahar bhejna. Wahi connectors banane padenge, ML nahi.

Chaho to main is breakdown ko ek page bana ke de sakta hoon jo team ke saath share ho sake, ya Stripe test-mode connector ka plan likh sakta hoon.

"""Planning for the refund worker.

The planner explains *how* it will handle a request and in what order. It does
**not** decide what is permitted — that authority belongs to
:func:`sololicense.domain.license.decide`, and the plan is built around the
decision it is handed. When an LLM key is configured the rationale is authored
by the model; otherwise a deterministic template is used. Either way the plan
is advisory text wrapped around a fixed, safe control flow.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from sololicense.agent.intake import complete
from sololicense.config import Config
from sololicense.domain.license import Decision, LicenseState
from sololicense.domain.models import RefundRequest
from sololicense.domain.task_classes import TaskClassSpec, get_spec

def _decision_steps(decision: Decision, spec: TaskClassSpec) -> list[str]:
    verify = f"Read orders.{spec.effect_column} back to verify the side effect."
    return {
        Decision.SUGGEST: [
            "Draft a recommendation for a human to act on.",
            "Do not touch the orders ledger.",
        ],
        Decision.DRAFT_FOR_APPROVAL: [
            f"Prepare the {spec.label.lower()} as a draft.",
            "Hold for human approval before any write.",
        ],
        Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE: [
            f"Execute the {spec.label.lower()} within the license ceiling.",
            verify,
            "Update the track record only if verification matches.",
        ],
        Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE_AUDITED: [
            f"Execute the {spec.label.lower()} under full autonomy.",
            verify,
            "Flag the run for post-hoc audit and update the track record.",
        ],
    }[decision]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Plan:
    rationale: str
    steps: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    source: str = "deterministic"


class Planner:
    def __init__(self, config: Config) -> None:
        self._config = config

    def plan(
        self, request: RefundRequest, decision: Decision, state: LicenseState
    ) -> Plan:
        return self._build_plan(request, decision, state)

content.text:
Roast taiyaar hai. Har criterion ko repo ke asli code aur artifacts se check kiya hai, sirf README ke daavon pe bharosa nahi kiya.

## Seedhi baat

**Verification aur state mein hum strong hain. Lekin "agent", "recovery" aur "evidence" mein judges hume pakad lenge.** Abhi project ek achhi tarah test kiya hua *safety pipeline* hai, jo ek *nakli refund* pe chal raha hai. Yeh woh "agent jo substantial task start se finish tak karta hai" nahi hai jo yeh track maang raha hai.

---

## Focus areas: kya cover hua, kya nahi

| Area | Status | Roast |
|---|---|---|
| **Planning** | 🔴 Kamzor | `planner.py` khud kehta hai ki plan "advisory text wrapped around a fixed, safe control flow" hai. Steps ek hardcoded dictionary (`_decision_steps`) se aate hain. LLM sirf rationale ka text likhta hai. Plan execution ko chalata hi nahi. |
| **Tool use** | 🔴 Kamzor | Sirf ek tool hai, `execute_refund`, jo SQLite ka ek column badhata hai. Woh tool **design se hi jhooth bolta hai** (`suppress_write` pe bhi `ok=True`). Koi asli API nahi, kaunsa tool chalana hai yeh choose karne ki baat hi nahi. |
| **State** | 🟢 Strong | SQLite, idempotency keys, har task class ka apna ladder, git ledger. Sahi hai. |
| **Context** | 🟡 Thoda | Intake message se order ID aur amount nikalta hai, prompt-injection guard bhi hai. Customer history, policy docs ya order details ka koi context andar nahi aata. |
| **Execution** | 🔴 Nahi | Ek run 84ms ka hai, ek hi DB write. "Long task" kuch nahi. |
| **Recovery** | 🟡 Aadha | Galti pakdi jaati hai → pause → insaan resume karta hai. Yeh **escalation** hai, recovery nahi. Agent khud kuch nahi karta: na retry, na reconcile, na rollback. |
| **Verification** | 🟢 Best part | Tool ka "success" ignore karke DB dobara padhna, plus 4 detections. Yahi asli USP hai. |
| **Iteration** | 🟡 Twist ke saath | Ek task ke andar "result se next step choose karna" nahi hai. Iteration sirf *runs ke beech* hota hai, jab level upar ya neeche hota hai. Woh smart hai, par judges ke definition se alag. |

## Requirements aur evidence checklist

| Requirement | Status | Roast |
|---|---|---|
| **The agent improved (before/after)** | 🟡 Risky | `artifacts/benchmark.md` "trust the tool" aur "verify" ka toggle compare karta hai, **kisi asli fix ka before/after nahi**. Faults bhi humne khud daale aur pakde bhi khud, toh benchmark circular lagta hai. Judges ko "humne bug dekha, fix kiya, phir se chalaya" wali kahani chahiye. |
| **neatlogs used** | 🟡 Daava hai, saboot nahi | Benchmark mein 5 trace IDs hain aur likha hai "these traces are in your neatlogs project". Lekin **koi clickable link nahi, koi screenshot nahi**. Judge ek bare hex ID ka kya karega? |
| **Entire used** | 🟡 Kamzor | 26 ledger commits **git** commits hain, Entire nahi. `entire checkpoint list` mein zyadatar `[temporary]` entries hain, aur repo mein entire-graph ka koi output saved nahi hai. Track ki line hai ki neatlogs aur Entire se agent ko *build aur improve* karna hai. Woh kahani kahin likhi nahi hai. |
| **cfo.ai plan** | 🔴 Missing in repo | `cfo/model.py` humara khud ka Python model hai, cfo.ai nahi. README kehta hai "plan built in cfo.ai via MCP", lekin koi link, export ya screenshot nahi hai. Model mein **inference/infra cost bhi nahi hai**, jabki cfo.ai ke example ka focus hi wahi hai. |
| **Agent recovers from failures** | 🟡 | Tour mein pause aur resume dikhta hai. Theek hai, lekin "what the agent did next" ka jawab hai "ruk gaya". |
| **Built in public (#neatHack)** | 🔴 Zero | Repo mein ek bhi link nahi. 15% weight wala criterion hai. |
| **Demo video** | 🔴 Nahi dikha | 20% weight. |
| **Code during hackathon** | 🟢 | 99 commits, 10–11 Oct, public repo. Lekin 26 `license(refund): demote L3 -> L0` app-generated commits main branch pe noise jaise lagte hain. |

## Weighted score ka mera andaza (honest, harsh)

| Category | Weight | Abhi |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | ~45/100: verification mast hai, lekin task tiny aur nakli hai |
| neatlogs + Entire + cfo.ai | 25% | ~40/100: teeno ka daava hai, saboot aadha |
| Demo video | 20% | 0 jab tak bana nahi |
| Building in public | 15% | 0 |
| Usefulness/originality | 10% | ~55/100: README khud maanta hai ki ladder naya nahi hai |

Itna polish wala landing page (shaders, signature pad, scramble text) aur agent ka core itna patla: **effort galat jagah laga hai.**

---

## Fix list (priority order, sabse zyada points per ghanta)

1. **Demo video + #neatHack posts** (35% weight, zero code). Abhi ek X/LinkedIn thread daalo, links README mein.
2. **Asli before/after story.** Commit `e896a9d` (rules wala intake injection ko flag karne laga) perfect hai. Purane commit pe injection message chalao → neatlogs trace mein galat refund dikhe. Fix ke baad → flagged trace. **Dono trace links + screenshots** README mein. Phir `entire checkpoint explain e896a9d` ka output bhi. Isse ek hi kahani mein neatlogs aur Entire dono ka "improve" wala proof mil jaata hai.
3. **cfo.ai ka saboot.** cfo.ai plan ka share link ya export, plus screenshots `docs/` mein. Inference cost per run bhi jodo.
4. **Recovery ko asli banao.** Quiet failure pakdi jaane pe agent pause karne se pehle **khud ek baar retry kare** (idempotency key ke saath), phir dobara verify kare. Fail ho tabhi escalate kare. Yeh ~1 function ka kaam hai aur "what the agent did next" ka strong jawab hai.
5. **Agent ko "substantial" banao.** Ek ticket pe multi-step loop: order lookup tool → policy check tool (return window, pehle ka refund) → refund ya credit choose karo → verify → customer ko reply draft karo. LLM agle tool ko pichhle result ke hisaab se choose kare. Isse planning, tool use, context aur iteration charo ek saath cover ho jaate hain.
6. **Stripe test mode** (agar time ho). Ek asli API se asli refund aur asli read-back. "Nakli refund" wali sabse badi kamzori khatam.
7. Ledger commits ko `ledger` branch ya alag repo mein daalo, taaki main ki history saaf rahe.

Main **#2 (before/after evidence)** aur **#4 (self-recovery retry)** se shuru karne ki salah dunga. Dono chhote hain, aur sabse zyada judge criteria ek saath hit karte hain. Bolo to start karta hoon.

    # --- helpers ---------------------------------------------------------

    def _authorize(
        self, state, request: RefundRequest, approved: bool
    ) -> Decision:
        """What the license authorises. A human approval grants execution at
        the level's audit posture (L3 keeps the audited variant)."""
        if approved and not state.quarantined:
            return (
                Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE_AUDITED
                if state.level is LicenseLevel.L3
                else Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE
            )
        return decide(
            state, request.amount,
            l2_ceiling=self._config.ceiling_for(state.task_class),
        )

    def _attempt(self, authorized: Decision, state, effects) -> Decision:
        """What the agent actually attempts. The policy-violation fault pushes
        it to auto-execute even when that is not authorised."""
        if effects.force_auto_execute:
            return (
                Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE_AUDITED
                if state.level is LicenseLevel.L3
                else Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE
            )
        return authorized

    def _do_execute(
        self, trace, request: RefundRequest, effects, task_class: str, column: str
    ) -> None:
        trace.span(
            f"tool.execute_{task_class}",
            order_id=request.order_id,
            amount=request.amount,
            suppress_write=effects.suppress_write,
        )
        tool_result = execute_refund(
            self._conn,
            order_id=request.order_id,
            amount=request.amount,
            suppress_write=effects.suppress_write,
            column=column,
        )
        # The tool's claim is recorded but explicitly marked untrusted.
        trace.span(
            "tool.result", ok=tool_result.ok, message=tool_result.message,
            trusted=False,
        )

    def _run_detections(
        self, *, authorized, attempted, intended_delta, result, duplicate
    ) -> list[Detection]:
        candidates = [
            rules.detect_policy_breach(authorized=authorized, attempted=attempted),
            rules.detect_duplicate_action(duplicate=duplicate),
            rules.detect_state_mismatch(
                intended_delta=intended_delta,
                actual_delta=result.actual_delta,
                verified=result.verified,
            ),
            rules.detect_missing_verification(verified=result.verified),
        ]
        return [d for d in candidates if d is not None]

    def _status(self, found, will_execute, authorized) -> RunStatus:
        if found:
            return RunStatus.DEMOTED
        if will_execute:
            return RunStatus.CLEAN
        if authorized is Decision.DRAFT_FOR_APPROVAL:
            return RunStatus.PENDING_APPROVAL
        return RunStatus.SUGGESTED

    def _persist_run(
        self, *, request, task_class, state_level, authorized, status, executed,
        result, idempotency_key, actor, effects, trace, plan,
    ) -> int:
        return insert_run(

            NewRun(

                order_id=request.order_id,

                fault_mode=effects.mode.value,
                trace_id=trace.trace_id,

    def _update_dial(
        self, task_class, status, found, run_id, trace_id, actor
    ) -> Transition:
        if status is RunStatus.DEMOTED:
            reason = "; ".join(d.message for d in found)
            return self._licenses.apply_detection(
                task_class, run_id=run_id, trace_id=trace_id, reason=reason, actor=actor
            )
        if status is RunStatus.CLEAN:
            return self._licenses.apply_clean_run(
                task_class, run_id=run_id, trace_id=trace_id, actor=actor
            )

        state = self._licenses.get_or_create(task_class)
        return Transition(old=state, new=state, kind="noop", git_sha=None)
"""The autonomy ladder and its state machine.

A *task class* (e.g. ``refund``) holds one :class:`LicenseState`. The agent may
only do what the current level permits. Levels are *earned* by consecutive
clean runs and *lost* immediately when a detection fires.

    L0  suggest only                       (human does everything)
    L1  draft + human approves each run
    L2  auto-execute under a dollar ceiling
    L3  full auto, post-hoc audit

Design notes
------------
* This module is pure: given the same inputs it always returns the same
  outputs and never touches a database, clock, or network. Persistence and
  side effects live in outer layers.
* A detection demotes the class straight to ``L0`` *and* quarantines it.
  While quarantined the class behaves at L0 and **cannot** auto-promote —
  only a human-reviewed evidence packet (``restore``) clears the quarantine.
  This is what makes recovery "with judgment, not blind retry".
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from enum import IntEnum


class LicenseLevel(IntEnum):
    """Rungs on the autonomy ladder. Ordered, so comparisons are meaningful."""

    L0 = 0  # suggest only
    L1 = 1  # draft + human approve
    L2 = 2  # auto under a threshold
    L3 = 3  # full auto with post-hoc audit

    @property
    def label(self) -> str:
        return {
            LicenseLevel.L0: "Suggest only",
            LicenseLevel.L1: "Draft + approve",
            LicenseLevel.L2: "Auto under ceiling",
            LicenseLevel.L3: "Full auto (audited)",
        }[self]


class Decision(IntEnum):
    """What the agent is permitted to do with a specific refund request."""

    SUGGEST = 0            # produce a recommendation only; no execution
    DRAFT_FOR_APPROVAL = 1  # prepare the change; a human must approve it
    AUTO_EXECUTE = 2        # execute now within policy
    AUTO_EXECUTE_AUDITED = 3  # execute now, flagged for post-hoc audit


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LicenseState:
    """Immutable snapshot of one task class's standing on the ladder.

    Instances are never mutated in place; every transition returns a new
    state, which keeps the state machine easy to reason about and test.
    """

    task_class: str
    level: LicenseLevel = LicenseLevel.L0
    consecutive_clean_runs: int = 0
    quarantined: bool = False
    # Level the class held before the most recent detection demotion, so a
    # reviewer can see "it fell from L2" when deciding how far to restore.
    demoted_from: LicenseLevel | None = None

    @property
    def effective_level(self) -> LicenseLevel:
        """Level actually in force. A quarantined class always acts at L0."""
        return LicenseLevel.L0 if self.quarantined else self.level


def decide(
    state: LicenseState,
    amount: float,
    *,
    l2_ceiling: float,
) -> Decision:
    """Resolve what the agent may do for a refund of ``amount`` dollars.

    This is the single authority on permissions. The worker must route every
    request through it and must never execute a side effect the returned
    :class:`Decision` does not authorise.
    """
    if amount < 0:
        raise ValueError("refund amount cannot be negative")

    level = state.effective_level

    if level is LicenseLevel.L0:
        return Decision.SUGGEST
    if level is LicenseLevel.L1:
        return Decision.DRAFT_FOR_APPROVAL
    if level is LicenseLevel.L2:
        # Auto only under the ceiling; anything above falls back to approval.
        if amount <= l2_ceiling:
            return Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE
        return Decision.DRAFT_FOR_APPROVAL
    return Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE_AUDITED  # L3


def record_clean_run(
    state: LicenseState,
    *,
    promotion_threshold: int,
) -> LicenseState:
    """Advance the track record after a verified-clean run.

    A quarantined class accrues no credit — it must be restored by a human
    first. Reaching ``promotion_threshold`` consecutive clean runs promotes
    the class one rung and resets the counter.
    """
    if state.quarantined:
        return state

    tally = state.consecutive_clean_runs + 1

    if state.level < LicenseLevel.L3 and tally >= promotion_threshold:
        return replace(
            state,
            level=LicenseLevel(state.level + 1),
            consecutive_clean_runs=0,
            demoted_from=None,
        )

    return replace(state, consecutive_clean_runs=tally, demoted_from=None)


def demote_on_detection(state: LicenseState) -> LicenseState:
    """Crash the class to L0 and quarantine it. Called the instant a
    detection fires. Idempotent in spirit: re-detecting a quarantined class
    keeps it quarantined and remembers the highest level it fell from."""
    fell_from = state.demoted_from if state.quarantined else state.level
    return replace(
        state,
        level=LicenseLevel.L0,
        consecutive_clean_runs=0,
        quarantined=True,
        demoted_from=fell_from,
    )


def restore(state: LicenseState, target: LicenseLevel) -> LicenseState:
    """Lift the quarantine and set the class to a human-chosen level.

    Only ever called after a reviewer has read the evidence packet, so the
    judgement lives with the human; this function just applies the decision.
    """
    return replace(
        state,
        level=target,
        consecutive_clean_runs=0,
        quarantined=False,
        demoted_from=None,
    )
"""Side-effect verification.

The one rule the whole system is built on: a tool's return value is never
evidence that something happened. To know whether a refund landed we read
``orders.refunded_amount`` back out of SQLite and compare the measured change
to what was intended."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass

from sololicense.db.repositories import orders as orders_repo


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class VerificationResult:
    """Outcome of reading a side effect back from the database."""

    before: float
    after: float
    intended_delta: float
    verified: bool  # True once a read-back was actually performed

    @property
    def actual_delta(self) -> float:
        return round(self.after - self.before, 2)

    @property
    def matched(self) -> bool:
        """Did the measured change equal the intended change?"""
        return abs(self.actual_delta - self.intended_delta) <= 1e-9


def read_refunded(
    conn: sqlite3.Connection, order_id: str, column: str = "refunded_amount"
) -> float:
    """Snapshot the authoritative side-effect amount for an order."""
    return orders_repo.get_effect_amount(conn, order_id, column)


def verify_refund(
    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
    *,
    order_id: str,
    before: float,
    intended_delta: float,
    column: str = "refunded_amount",
) -> VerificationResult:
    """Read the side effect back and compare it to what was intended."""
    after = read_refunded(conn, order_id, column)
    return VerificationResult(
        before=before,
        after=after,
        intended_delta=intended_delta,
        verified=True,
    )


def missing_refund_verification(
    *, before: float, intended_delta: float
) -> VerificationResult:
    """Represent an execution whose read-back did not run or complete."""
    return VerificationResult(
        before=before,
        after=before,
        intended_delta=intended_delta,
        verified=False,
    )
"""Custom detection rules.

These are the load-bearing checks that make autonomy *earned*: each one, when
it fires, demotes the task class. They are pure functions over observed facts
so they can be unit-tested and so the same logic both (a) emits a neatlogs
detection event and (b) is mirrored as a local rule — the documented mapping
when a live neatlogs key is absent.

Three rules, matching the spec:
    state_mismatch        the DB side effect did not match what was intended
    missing_verification  the agent reported done without reading SQLite back
    policy_breach         the attempted action exceeded the current license
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from sololicense.domain.license import Decision

CRITICAL = "critical"
WARNING = "warning"

# Decisions that actually touch the world.
_EXECUTING = (Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE, Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE_AUDITED)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Detection:
    rule: str
    severity: str
    message: str


def detect_state_mismatch(
    *, intended_delta: float, actual_delta: float, verified: bool = True
) -> Detection | None:
    """Fire when the verified change in ``refunded_amount`` does not equal the
    refund the agent intended to make (the signature of a quiet failure)."""
    if not verified:
        return None
    if abs(intended_delta - actual_delta) > 1e-9:
        return Detection(
            rule="state_mismatch",
            severity=CRITICAL,
            message=(
                f"Intended refund delta ${intended_delta:.2f} but SQLite moved "
                f"${actual_delta:.2f}. Tool response cannot be trusted."
            ),
        )
    return None


def detect_missing_verification(*, verified: bool) -> Detection | None:
    """Fire when an execution completed but no read-back verification ran."""
    if not verified:
        return Detection(
            rule="missing_verification",
            severity=CRITICAL,
            message="Execution reported complete without verifying SQLite state.",
        )
    return None


def detect_duplicate_action(*, duplicate: bool) -> Detection | None:
    """Fire when a retry tries to execute an already-executed action key."""
    if duplicate:
        return Detection(
            rule="duplicate_action",
            severity=CRITICAL,
            message="Idempotency key already executed; duplicate action blocked.",
        )
    return None


def detect_policy_breach(
    *, authorized: Decision, attempted: Decision
) -> Detection | None:
    """Fire when the agent executed beyond what the license authorised.

    The authorised decision already folds in level, amount, and the L2 ceiling
    (see :func:`sololicense.domain.license.decide`), so the rule is simply:
    the agent executed while the license said suggest or draft only.
    """
    if attempted in _EXECUTING and authorized not in _EXECUTING:
        return Detection(
            rule="policy_breach",
            severity=CRITICAL,
            message=(
                f"Agent attempted {attempted.name} but the license only "
                f"authorised {authorized.name}."
            ),
        )
    return None

            state, request.amount,
            l2_ceiling=self._config.ceiling_for(state.task_class),
        )

    def _attempt(self, authorized: Decision, state, effects) -> Decision:
        """What the agent actually attempts. The policy-violation fault pushes
        it to auto-execute even when that is not authorised."""
        if effects.force_auto_execute:
            return (
                Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE_AUDITED
                if state.level is LicenseLevel.L3
                else Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE
            )
        return authorized

    def _do_execute(
        self, trace, request: RefundRequest, effects, task_class: str, column: str
    ) -> None:
        trace.span(
            f"tool.execute_{task_class}",
            order_id=request.order_id,
            amount=request.amount,
            suppress_write=effects.suppress_write,
        )
        tool_result = execute_refund(
            self._conn,
            order_id=request.order_id,
            amount=request.amount,
            suppress_write=effects.suppress_write,
            column=column,
        )
        # The tool's claim is recorded but explicitly marked untrusted.
        trace.span(
            "tool.result", ok=tool_result.ok, message=tool_result.message,
            trusted=False,
        )

    def _run_detections(
        self, *, authorized, attempted, intended_delta, result, duplicate
    ) -> list[Detection]:
        candidates = [
            rules.detect_policy_breach(authorized=authorized, attempted=attempted),
            rules.detect_duplicate_action(duplicate=duplicate),
            rules.detect_state_mismatch(
                intended_delta=intended_delta,
                actual_delta=result.actual_delta,
                verified=result.verified,
            ),
            rules.detect_missing_verification(verified=result.verified),
        ]
        return [d for d in candidates if d is not None]

    def _status(self, found, will_execute, authorized) -> RunStatus:
        if found:
            return RunStatus.DEMOTED
        if will_execute:
            return RunStatus.CLEAN
        if authorized is Decision.DRAFT_FOR_APPROVAL:
            return RunStatus.PENDING_APPROVAL
        return RunStatus.SUGGESTED

    def _persist_run(
        self, *, request, task_class, state_level, authorized, status, executed,
        result, idempotency_key, actor, effects, trace, plan,
    ) -> int:
        return insert_run(
            self._conn,
            NewRun(
                task_class=task_class,
                order_id=request.order_id,
                requested_amount=request.amount,
                level_at_run=int(state_level),
                decision=authorized.name,
                status=status.value,
                executed=executed and status is not RunStatus.SUGGESTED,
                before_refunded=result.before,
                after_refunded=result.after,
                idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
                actor_id=actor.actor_id,
                actor_role=actor.role.value,
                fault_mode=effects.mode.value,
                trace_id=trace.trace_id,
                notes=plan.rationale,
            ),
        )

    def _update_dial(
        self, task_class, status, found, run_id, trace_id, actor
    ) -> Transition:
        if status is RunStatus.DEMOTED:
            reason = "; ".join(d.message for d in found)
            return self._licenses.apply_detection(
                task_class, run_id=run_id, trace_id=trace_id, reason=reason, actor=actor
            )
        if status is RunStatus.CLEAN:
            return self._licenses.apply_clean_run(
                task_class, run_id=run_id, trace_id=trace_id, actor=actor
            )
        # Suggestions and pending approvals do not move the dial.
        state = self._licenses.get_or_create(task_class)
        return Transition(old=state, new=state, kind="noop", git_sha=None)
"""The autonomy ladder and its state machine.

A *task class* (e.g. ``refund``) holds one :class:`LicenseState`. The agent may
only do what the current level permits. Levels are *earned* by consecutive
clean runs and *lost* immediately when a detection fires.

    L0  suggest only                       (human does everything)
    L1  draft + human approves each run
    L2  auto-execute under a dollar ceiling
    L3  full auto, post-hoc audit

Design notes
------------
* This module is pure: given the same inputs it always returns the same
  outputs and never touches a database, clock, or network. Persistence and
  side effects live in outer layers.
* A detection demotes the class straight to ``L0`` *and* quarantines it.
  While quarantined the class behaves at L0 and **cannot** auto-promote —
  only a human-reviewed evidence packet (``restore``) clears the quarantine.
  This is what makes recovery "with judgment, not blind retry".
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from enum import IntEnum


class LicenseLevel(IntEnum):
    """Rungs on the autonomy ladder. Ordered, so comparisons are meaningful."""

    L0 = 0  # suggest only
    L1 = 1  # draft + human approve
    L2 = 2  # auto under a threshold
    L3 = 3  # full auto with post-hoc audit

    @property
    def label(self) -> str:
        return {
            LicenseLevel.L0: "Suggest only",
            LicenseLevel.L1: "Draft + approve",
            LicenseLevel.L2: "Auto under ceiling",
            LicenseLevel.L3: "Full auto (audited)",
        }[self]


class Decision(IntEnum):
    """What the agent is permitted to do with a specific refund request."""

    SUGGEST = 0            # produce a recommendation only; no execution
    DRAFT_FOR_APPROVAL = 1  # prepare the change; a human must approve it
    AUTO_EXECUTE = 2        # execute now within policy
    AUTO_EXECUTE_AUDITED = 3  # execute now, flagged for post-hoc audit


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LicenseState:
    """Immutable snapshot of one task class's standing on the ladder.

    Instances are never mutated in place; every transition returns a new
    state, which keeps the state machine easy to reason about and test.
    """

    task_class: str
    level: LicenseLevel = LicenseLevel.L0
    consecutive_clean_runs: int = 0
    quarantined: bool = False
    # Level the class held before the most recent detection demotion, so a
    # reviewer can see "it fell from L2" when deciding how far to restore.
    demoted_from: LicenseLevel | None = None

    @property
    def effective_level(self) -> LicenseLevel:
        """Level actually in force. A quarantined class always acts at L0."""
        return LicenseLevel.L0 if self.quarantined else self.level


def decide(
    state: LicenseState,
    amount: float,
    *,
    l2_ceiling: float,
) -> Decision:
    """Resolve what the agent may do for a refund of ``amount`` dollars.

    This is the single authority on permissions. The worker must route every
    request through it and must never execute a side effect the returned
    :class:`Decision` does not authorise.
    """
    if amount < 0:
        raise ValueError("refund amount cannot be negative")

    level = state.effective_level

    if level is LicenseLevel.L0:
        return Decision.SUGGEST
    if level is LicenseLevel.L1:
        return Decision.DRAFT_FOR_APPROVAL
    if level is LicenseLevel.L2:
        # Auto only under the ceiling; anything above falls back to approval.
        if amount <= l2_ceiling:
            return Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE
        return Decision.DRAFT_FOR_APPROVAL
    return Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE_AUDITED  # L3


def record_clean_run(
    state: LicenseState,
    *,
    promotion_threshold: int,
) -> LicenseState:
    """Advance the track record after a verified-clean run.

    A quarantined class accrues no credit — it must be restored by a human
    first. Reaching ``promotion_threshold`` consecutive clean runs promotes
    the class one rung and resets the counter.
    """
    if state.quarantined:
        return state

    tally = state.consecutive_clean_runs + 1

    if state.level < LicenseLevel.L3 and tally >= promotion_threshold:
        return replace(
            state,
            level=LicenseLevel(state.level + 1),
            consecutive_clean_runs=0,
            demoted_from=None,
        )

    return replace(state, consecutive_clean_runs=tally, demoted_from=None)


def demote_on_detection(state: LicenseState) -> LicenseState:
    """Crash the class to L0 and quarantine it. Called the instant a
    detection fires. Idempotent in spirit: re-detecting a quarantined class
    keeps it quarantined and remembers the highest level it fell from."""
    fell_from = state.demoted_from if state.quarantined else state.level
    return replace(
        state,
        level=LicenseLevel.L0,
        consecutive_clean_runs=0,
        quarantined=True,
        demoted_from=fell_from,
    )


def restore(state: LicenseState, target: LicenseLevel) -> LicenseState:
    """Lift the quarantine and set the class to a human-chosen level.

    Only ever called after a reviewer has read the evidence packet, so the
    judgement lives with the human; this function just applies the decision.
    """
    return replace(
        state,
        level=target,
        consecutive_clean_runs=0,
        quarantined=False,
        demoted_from=None,
    )
"""Side-effect verification.

The one rule the whole system is built on: a tool's return value is never
evidence that something happened. To know whether a refund landed we read
``orders.refunded_amount`` back out of SQLite and compare the measured change
to what was intended."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass

from sololicense.db.repositories import orders as orders_repo


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class VerificationResult:
    """Outcome of reading a side effect back from the database."""

    before: float
    after: float
    intended_delta: float
    verified: bool  # True once a read-back was actually performed

    @property
    def actual_delta(self) -> float:
        return round(self.after - self.before, 2)

    @property
    def matched(self) -> bool:
        """Did the measured change equal the intended change?"""
        return abs(self.actual_delta - self.intended_delta) <= 1e-9


def read_refunded(
    conn: sqlite3.Connection, order_id: str, column: str = "refunded_amount"
) -> float:
    """Snapshot the authoritative side-effect amount for an order."""
    return orders_repo.get_effect_amount(conn, order_id, column)


def verify_refund(
    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
    *,
    order_id: str,
    before: float,
    intended_delta: float,
    column: str = "refunded_amount",
) -> VerificationResult:
    """Read the side effect back and compare it to what was intended."""
    after = read_refunded(conn, order_id, column)
    return VerificationResult(
        before=before,
        after=after,
        intended_delta=intended_delta,
        verified=True,
    )


def missing_refund_verification(
    *, before: float, intended_delta: float
) -> VerificationResult:
    """Represent an execution whose read-back did not run or complete."""
    return VerificationResult(
        before=before,
        after=before,
        intended_delta=intended_delta,
        verified=False,
    )
"""Custom detection rules.

These are the load-bearing checks that make autonomy *earned*: each one, when
it fires, demotes the task class. They are pure functions over observed facts
so they can be unit-tested and so the same logic both (a) emits a neatlogs
detection event and (b) is mirrored as a local rule — the documented mapping
when a live neatlogs key is absent.

Three rules, matching the spec:
    state_mismatch        the DB side effect did not match what was intended
    missing_verification  the agent reported done without reading SQLite back
    policy_breach         the attempted action exceeded the current license
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from sololicense.domain.license import Decision

CRITICAL = "critical"
WARNING = "warning"

# Decisions that actually touch the world.
_EXECUTING = (Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE, Decision.AUTO_EXECUTE_AUDITED)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Detection:
    rule: str
    severity: str
    message: str


def detect_state_mismatch(
    *, intended_delta: float, actual_delta: float, verified: bool = True
) -> Detection | None:
    """Fire when the verified change in ``refunded_amount`` does not equal the
    refund the agent intended to make (the signature of a quiet failure)."""
    if not verified:
        return None
    if abs(intended_delta - actual_delta) > 1e-9:
        return Detection(
            rule="state_mismatch",
            severity=CRITICAL,
            message=(
                f"Intended refund delta ${intended_delta:.2f} but SQLite moved "
                f"${actual_delta:.2f}. Tool response cannot be trusted."
            ),
        )
    return None


def detect_missing_verification(*, verified: bool) -> Detection | None:
    """Fire when an execution completed but no read-back verification ran."""
    if not verified:
        return Detection(
            rule="missing_verification",
            severity=CRITICAL,
            message="Execution reported complete without verifying SQLite state.",
        )
    return None


def detect_duplicate_action(*, duplicate: bool) -> Detection | None:
    """Fire when a retry tries to execute an already-executed action key."""
    if duplicate:
        return Detection(
            rule="duplicate_action",
            severity=CRITICAL,
            message="Idempotency key already executed; duplicate action blocked.",
        )
    return None


def detect_policy_breach(
    *, authorized: Decision, attempted: Decision
) -> Detection | None:
    """Fire when the agent executed beyond what the license authorised.

    The authorised decision already folds in level, amount, and the L2 ceiling
    (see :func:`sololicense.domain.license.decide`), so the rule is simply:
    the agent executed while the license said suggest or draft only.
    """
    if attempted in _EXECUTING and authorized not in _EXECUTING:
        return Detection(
            rule="policy_breach",
            severity=CRITICAL,
            message=(
                f"Agent attempted {attempted.name} but the license only "
                f"authorised {authorized.name}."
            ),
        )
    return None
